The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of deceased Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
2 Srinivas, in the road traffic accident that took place on 23.06.2023.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 23.06.2023 at about 4.45 p.m., when deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-X-9149, on Srirangapatna-K.R. Pet Main Road, Near Damadahalli,
Sannappana Javaregowda Jameenu, Mandya District, at that time, suddenly the driver of Maruti Swift D'Zire Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 42-A-5386 came from behind by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, caused the accident and as a result, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries and died on the spot.

It is contended that, immediately after the accident, deceased was shifted to Pandavapura Government hospital wherein post- mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that the deceased was working as Agriculture cum Sericulturist and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A- 5386.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have entered appearance through their learned counsels and the 2 nd respondent filed objection statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
The 2 nd respondent has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

It has contended that the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-06-X-9149 was riding the said vehicle without valid driving licence and insurance policy and therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation.

It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A-5386 was not holding valid driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident and hence, it is not liable to pay the compensation.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A-5386 and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It has further contended that the interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-

3 ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri.
Srinivas?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that on On 23.06.2023 at about 4.45 p.m., when deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-X-9149, on Srirangapatna-K.R. Pet main road, Near Damadahalli, Sannappana Javaregowda Jameenu, Mandya District, at that time, suddenly the driver of Maruti Swift D'Zire Car bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A- 5386 came from behind by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, caused the accident and as a result, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries and died on the spot?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4

. What order or Award?
8.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Ex.P1 to 11.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R1 & 2 documents.

9. Heard the arguments.
10.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

In the affirmative,

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 ... As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1: The petitioners claim that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief- examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The School Admission certificate and Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P8, 9 to 11 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased Srinivas.

Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
4 dependents of deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, I answer to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.2 :

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 23.06.2023 at about 4.45 p.m., when deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-X-9149, on Srirangapatna-K.R. Pet main road, Near Damadahalli, Sannappana Javaregowda Jameenu, Mandya District, at that time,
suddenly the driver of Maruti Swift D'Zire Car bearing Reg. No. KA-42-A-5386 came from behind by driving it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, caused the accident and as a result, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries and died on the spot.
It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the car driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

13. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, Spot Mahzar, IMV Report, Inquest Report, P.M. Report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

On the other hand, respondent have examined its official as RW.1 and she got marked authorisation letter and Insurance policy as per Ex.R1 and R2.
14.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of car.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
5

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

15. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Damadahalli, Sannappana Javaregowda Jameenu, Mandya District, when the driver of car came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased's motorcycle and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 it reflects that deceased was proceeding on his lane on the left side of the road and suddenly the offending car came in a negligent manner from back side of the deceased's motorcycle and hit the motor cyclist.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of car coming in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.4 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P7 was also filed as against the driver of the car.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 and 5 coupled with Ex.P.7 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the car.

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the driver of the car is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the car and he was charge sheeted.

Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
6 17.

Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing to be elicited from her mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P5 coupled with Ex.P7 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-5386 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Srinivas, was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending Car bearing Reg. No.
KA-42-A-5386.
The petitioner No.1 is stated to be the wife, petitioners No. 2 & 3 are stated to be children of the deceased.
19. The petitioners have contended that the deceased was an Agriculture cum Sericulturist and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not produced any document to show the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased, the court has to take into consideration the notional income.
Considering the work of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month.
20. It is stated that the deceased was aged 55 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced the notarized copy of School Admission Certificate of the deceased at Ex.P8 which shows the date of birth as 20.06.1968.
The accident was occurred on 23.06.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 55 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '11'.
21.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 55 years.
Therefore, in this case, 10% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

As such, if 10% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,600/- a.m. (Rs.16,000/-
+ 1,600/- i.e. 10%).
The deceased died leaving behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,734/- p.m.(Rs.17,600 - Rs.5,866 = Rs.11,734/-).

Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
7 22.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,734/- p.m. and the multiplier '11' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.15,48,888/- (Rs.11,734 X 12 X 14).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,48,888/- under the head of loss of dependency.

23. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.

In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are major children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father, as well as Petitioner No.4 towards deceased her son.

Therefore,
petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

25. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.15,48,888/-

2 . Towards loss of Consortium to Rs.44,000/-
the petitioner No.1 3.
Towards loss to estate Rs.16,500/-

4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.16,500/- body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5. Towards loss of Filial Rs.88,000/-
 consortium to petitioner No.2 &
 3(Each Rs.44,000/-)

Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
8

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,13,888/-.
26.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1 st petitioner is the widow, petitioners No.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 to 3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 70:15:15.
27.
The petitioners are claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.2 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
28. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Car bearing Reg. No.
KA-42-A-5386.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
RW.1 in her cross examination admits that the offending vehicle was having valid insurance policy and the driver of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-42-A-5386 was having valid driving license.
Ex.R2 also reflects that insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident in respect of the offending Car.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,13,888/-(Rupees Seventeen lakhs thirteen thousand eight hundred and eighty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 70%
 Petitioner No.2 - 15%
 Petitioner No.3 - 15%
Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
9

Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share amount apportioned in favour of petitioners No.2 and 3 shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 it reflects that deceased was proceeding on his lane on the left side of the road and suddenly the offending car came in a negligent manner from back side of the deceased's motorcycle and hit the motor cyclist.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of car coming in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 and 5 coupled with Ex.P.7 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the car.
16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.
Even in the instant case the driver of the car is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the car and he was charge sheeted.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence with regard to the income of the deceased, the court has to take into consideration the notional income.
Considering the work of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 55 years.
As such, if 10% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,600/- a.m. (Rs.16,000/-
+ 1,600/- i.e. 10%).
The deceased died leaving behind 3 dependents.
In this case, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are major children of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,734/- p.m. and the multiplier '11' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.15,48,888/- (Rs.11,734 X 12 X 14).
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,48,888/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
24.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father, as well as Petitioner No.4 towards deceased her son.
Therefore,
petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
25. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.15,48,888/-
2 . Towards loss of Consortium to Rs.44,000/-
the petitioner No.1 3.
Towards loss to estate Rs.16,500/-
4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.16,500/- body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5. Towards loss of Filial Rs.88,000/-
 consortium to petitioner No.2 &
 3(Each Rs.44,000/-)
Total Rs.17,13,888/-
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,13,888/-.
26.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 to 3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 70:15:15.
27.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,13,888/-(Rupees Seventeen lakhs thirteen thousand eight hundred and eighty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 70%
 Petitioner No.2 - 15%
 Petitioner No.3 - 15%
Shobha vs Rajath K on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33814768/
9
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share amount apportioned in favour of petitioners No.2 and 3 shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
